drivingQuestion: What does 'he has done nothing' mean for intentionally separated teruma from impure produce?
outcomeNote: the unit ends after Rav Ḥisda's reading; the rival reading and the link to the mamzer ruling follow in the next unit

segments.he: הַוָּלָד מַמְזֵר. תְּנַן הָתָם: אֵין תּוֹרְמִין מִן הַטָּמֵא עַל הַטָּהוֹר, וְאִם תָּרַם, בְּשׁוֹגֵג — תְּרוּמָתוֹ תְּרוּמָה, בְּמֵזִיד — לֹא עָשָׂה וְלֹא כְּלוּם. מַאי לֹא עָשָׂה וְלֹא כְּלוּם? אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: לֹא עָשָׂה וְלֹא כְּלוּם כׇּל עִיקָּר, דַּאֲפִילּוּ הָהֻיא גְּרִיוָא הָדַר לְטִיבְלֵיהּ.
segments.en: § The mishna taught that «the child» of either of the men is «a mamzer.» To clarify this issue, the Gemara cites a different discussion. «We learned» in a mishna «elsewhere» (Terumot 2:2): «One may not separate» teruma «from ritually impure» produce in order «to» exempt «ritually pure» food, «and if he separated» teruma from impure food «unwittingly, his teruma is» considered «teruma.» If he acted «intentionally, he has done nothing,» that is, his action is of no effect. The Sages debated: «What» is the meaning of the expression: «He has done nothing? Rav Ḥisda said: He has done nothing at all,» meaning «that even that griva» of produce he set aside as teruma «returns to» its former «untithed» state, as his entire act is completely disregarded.
